easy.def: To swerve.

more.def: To change direction suddenly.
examples: The car veered to avoid the dog.
The path veers sharply toward the creek.
The ball veered off to the side.

easy.def: A person who eats no animal foods.

more.def: A person who does not eat or use anything that comes from animals.
examples: My cousin is a vegan and eats only plants.
A vegan does not eat eggs or cheese.
She became a vegan last year.

easy.def: A plant that you eat, like a carrot.

more.def: A plant or part of a plant that people eat, such as a carrot, a bean or a potato.
examples: She grew vegetables in the garden.
We had soup full of vegetables.

easy.def: A person who does not eat meat.

more.def: A person who chooses not to eat meat, and eats plants, such as fruits and vegetables, instead.
examples: My cousin is a vegetarian and eats a lot of beans and rice.
The school lunch menu has a choice for vegetarians each day.
A vegetarian might eat vegetables, fruit, nuts and sometimes eggs and cheese.

easy.def: Made without meat.

more.def: Having no meat in it, or made for people who do not eat meat.
examples: We ordered a vegetarian pizza with peppers and mushrooms.
The restaurant has a vegetarian menu with many choices.
My grandmother made a vegetarian chili full of beans.

easy.def: Plants and trees growing in a place.
examples: The island has lots of vegetation.

more.def: The plants and trees that grow in a place.
examples: Little vegetation grows in the desert.
The hikers pushed through the dense vegetation.

easy.def: A short word for vegetable.

more.def: A short, casual word for a vegetable.
examples: We ate carrots, peas and other veggies.
She dipped a veggie in the sauce.

easy.def: A thing that takes people from place to place, like a car or bus.
examples: A truck is a big vehicle.
A bus is a vehicle for many people.

more.def: A machine such as a car, bus, or truck that carries people or things.
examples: Only emergency vehicles may park in front of the hospital.
A bicycle is a vehicle with two wheels.
The road was closed to all vehicles during the parade.

easy.def: A thin cloth that covers the face or head.

more.def: A thin piece of cloth worn over the face or head, often at a wedding.
examples: The bride wore a white veil.
A lace veil covered her hair.
A veil of mist hung over the field.

easy.def: A tube that carries blood to your heart.
examples: I can see a vein in my arm.

more.def: One of the tubes in the body that carry blood back to the heart.
examples: A vein in my arm is blue.
Blood flows through your veins to your heart.
The nurse found a vein to take blood.

easy.def: A line on a leaf.

more.def: One of the thin lines that you can see on a leaf.
examples: The leaf had green veins on its back.
I traced the vein with my finger.
Water moves through the veins of the leaf.

easy.def: Speed in a direction.

more.def: The speed of something in a particular direction.
examples: The ball left the bat at high velocity.
Scientists measure the velocity of wind.
A rocket needs great velocity to leave Earth.

easy.def: A very soft material.

more.def: A thick, soft cloth that is smooth on one side.
examples: The couch was covered in red velvet.
Velvet feels soft against your skin.
The queen wore a velvet robe.

easy.def: A soft cloth that feels like velvet.

more.def: A soft, thick cloth.
examples: The toy rabbit was made of velveteen.
The velveteen cushion was soft to touch.

easy.def: To sell things.

more.def: To sell things, especially from a machine or a stand.
examples: The machine vends snacks and drinks.
He vended fruit from a cart.
The old man vends balloons at the park.

easy.def: A person who sells things outside, like at a fair.

more.def: A person who sells things, especially from a stand, a cart or a stall.
examples: The vendor sold popcorn and lemonade at the fair.
A street vendor sold hot pretzels from a cart.
The vendors set up their stalls at the market.

easy.def: Old and respected.

more.def: Respected because of age and wisdom.
examples: A venerable oak stood in the square.
The venerable teacher had taught for fifty years.
A venerable old building stood on the hill.

easy.def: The meat of a deer.

more.def: The meat of a deer used for food.
examples: We had venison stew for dinner.
In old stories, the lord served venison at his feast.

easy.def: Poison that a snake or spider puts in you when it bites.

more.def: A poison that some snakes, spiders and insects put into another animal's body when they bite or sting.
examples: The rattlesnake has venom that can make a person very sick.
Bees put a tiny bit of venom into your skin when they sting.
Scientists use venom from some snakes to make medicines.

easy.def: Able to hurt with poison.

more.def: Able to give a poisonous bite or sting.
examples: The snake is venomous, so stay away.
A venomous spider hid in the corner.

easy.def: An opening that lets air or smoke out.
examples: The air comes out of the vent.
A vent is on the wall.

more.def: An opening that lets air, gas or smoke pass through.
examples: Warm air blew out of the vent.
The kitchen has a vent over the stove.
Steam rose from the vent in the street.

easy.def: To let fresh air in.

more.def: To let fresh air move through a space.
examples: Open the window to ventilate the room.

easy.def: Fresh air coming into a room.

more.def: A system or a way of letting fresh air move in and out of a room or building.
examples: The room needs better ventilation because it feels stuffy.
We opened the windows for ventilation.
A ventilation fan pulls the cooking smells out of the kitchen.

easy.def: A fan or opening that lets fresh air in.
examples: The ventilator is on the roof.

more.def: A device or opening that lets fresh air flow into a room.
examples: The ventilator hummed on the ceiling.
A ventilator keeps the barn fresh.
Open the ventilator to get fresh air.

easy.def: A person who makes a puppet seem to talk.
examples: The ventriloquist made the doll talk.

more.def: A performer who speaks without moving the lips so that a puppet seems to be talking.
examples: The ventriloquist made her puppet talk and joke.
We laughed at the ventriloquist's funny show.
The ventriloquist spoke in two voices.

easy.def: To go somewhere that may be risky.

more.def: To go somewhere or try something that is risky or new.
examples: We ventured into the dark woods.
She ventured outside in the storm.
He ventured a guess about the answer.

easy.def: A place where an event happens.

more.def: The place where an event, such as a concert or game, is held.
examples: The venue for the game was the new stadium.

easy.def: The bright planet next to Earth.
examples: Venus shines in the evening sky.
We found Venus with a telescope.

more.def: The second planet from the sun, which is covered in thick clouds and is hotter than any other planet.
examples: Venus is often the brightest object in the sky after the sun and moon.
A day on Venus is longer than a year there.
Scientists have sent space probes to study the clouds of Venus.

easy.def: A roofed place along the side of a house.

more.def: A porch with a roof along the outside of a house.
examples: We ate lunch on the shady veranda.
The old house had a wide veranda all the way around.
Rain tapped on the roof of the veranda.

easy.def: A word that tells what someone does.
examples: A verb is an action word.

more.def: A word that tells what someone or something does or is, such as run, think or be.
examples: The word "jump" is a verb because it shows an action.
In the sentence "She sings well," the verb is "sings."

easy.def: Said out loud, with words.

more.def: Using spoken words rather than writing, or having to do with words.
examples: The coach gave us verbal instructions instead of a written plan.
A verbal promise is one that is spoken aloud, not written down.
Reading aloud is a good way to practice verbal skills.

easy.def: Word for word.

more.def: In exactly the same words.
examples: The note copied the speech verbatim.

easy.def: Using too many words.

more.def: Using more words than are needed.
examples: His speech was long and verbose.
The verbose note could have been shorter.

easy.def: The decision made at the end of a trial.

more.def: The decision that a jury or a judge gives at the end of a trial, or any final opinion or judgment.
examples: The jury gave its verdict after a long talk.
The verdict was that the man was not guilty.
My verdict on the new movie is that it is great.

easy.def: The point just before something happens.
examples: She was on the verge of tears.
We are on the verge of winning.
He was on the verge of laughing.

more.def: The point at which something is just about to happen or start.
examples: The baby was on the verge of tears.
We were on the verge of winning the game.
The old bridge is on the verge of falling.

easy.def: Able to be proved true.

more.def: Able to be checked and shown to be true.
examples: The facts in the report are verifiable.
A verifiable fact can be looked up.
Her claim was verifiable, so we believed her.

easy.def: To check that something is true.

more.def: To make sure that something is true or correct.
examples: I verified my answer by checking the book.
She verified the facts before writing.
He verified the time on the clock.

easy.def: A bright red-orange color.

more.def: A bright red color with a touch of orange.
examples: The sunset was a brilliant vermilion.
The artist painted a vermilion sun.

easy.def: Small animals like rats and bugs that cause trouble.

more.def: Small animals or insects, such as rats, mice and fleas, that are harmful or carry disease and cause trouble.
examples: The farmer put a lid on the grain to keep out vermin.
Rats and fleas are called vermin because they can spread disease.
A cat in the barn helps keep the vermin away.

easy.def: Able to do many things.

more.def: Able to be used in many ways or do many different things.
examples: A rope is a versatile tool.
She is a versatile player who can play any position.
The versatile cloth can be used as a scarf or a bag.

easy.def: A group of lines in a poem or song.

more.def: A group of lines in a poem or song, or a poem.
examples: The poem's last verse made everyone smile.
She read the first verse aloud.
I memorized a verse of the poem.

easy.def: A different form of something.
examples: I read the short version of the story.

more.def: A form of something that is a little different from others.
examples: The movie is a new version of an old fairy tale.
The new version of the game has better graphics.
Each person told a different version of what happened.

easy.def: Against.
examples: The game is red versus blue.

more.def: Used to show two sides in a game or choice.
examples: Tonight is the game of our school versus yours.
The vote was cats versus dogs.
The contest was speed versus skill.

easy.def: One of the small bones in your back.

more.def: One of the small bones that are joined together to make the backbone.
examples: Each vertebra is a small bone in your backbone.
A giraffe has only seven vertebrae in its long neck, just like a person.
The doctor pointed to a vertebra in the picture of the spine.

easy.def: An animal with bones inside it.

more.def: An animal that has a backbone, such as a fish, bird or human.
examples: Birds, reptiles and humans are all vertebrates.

easy.def: The corner where two lines meet.
examples: Each corner of a square is a vertex.

more.def: The point where two lines or edges of a shape meet, forming a corner.
examples: The vertex of an angle is where two sides meet.

easy.def: Straight up and down.

more.def: Going straight up and down, like a flagpole or a tree trunk, not flat or sideways.
examples: Draw a vertical line from the top of the page to the bottom.
The flagpole stood vertical against the sky.
The climbers inched up the vertical wall of rock.

easy.def: Straight up and down.

more.def: In a direction that goes straight up and down.
examples: The pole stood vertically in the ground.
The books were stacked vertically on the shelf.

easy.def: A dizzy feeling when you are up high.
examples: The tall tower gave him vertigo.

more.def: A feeling of dizziness, as if everything is spinning, often when you look down from a height.
examples: He felt vertigo at the top of the tower.
Vertigo made her step back from the edge.
She had vertigo when she looked down.

easy.def: A lot, or much.

more.def: To a high degree, or extremely.
examples: The whale is a very large animal.
It was a very quiet night in the forest.
He was very proud of his drawing.

easy.def: A ship or large boat.
examples: A vessel is in the bay.

more.def: A ship or large boat.
examples: The vessel sailed out of the harbor.
A fishing vessel returned at dawn.
The huge vessel carried goods across the ocean.

easy.def: A bowl or bottle for water.
examples: Put the water in the vessel.

more.def: A container such as a bowl or bottle, used for holding liquid.
examples: A jug is a vessel for carrying water.
The potter made a clay vessel.
Pour the milk into a clean vessel.

easy.def: A short top with no sleeves.

more.def: A piece of clothing with no sleeves that is worn over a shirt.
examples: He wore a warm vest over his shirt.
The workers wear a bright vest.
I zipped up my life vest.

easy.def: A small room or hall just inside the front door.

more.def: A small entrance hall just inside the front door of a building.
examples: We took off our coats in the vestibule.

easy.def: A doctor for animals.
examples: We took the cat to the vet.

more.def: A short word for veterinarian, a doctor who treats animals.
examples: The vet checked my dog's ears.
We took the cat to the vet for a shot.
The vet fixed the bird's wing.

easy.def: A person who served in the army.

more.def: A person who has served in the military, or someone with a lot of experience.
examples: My grandpa is a veteran of the navy.
She is a veteran teacher with twenty years of experience.

easy.def: A doctor for animals.
examples: The veterinarian gave the dog a shot.
I want to be a veterinarian.

more.def: A doctor who takes care of animals and treats them when they are sick or hurt.
examples: The veterinarian listened to the puppy's heart.
A veterinarian helped the cow that was sick.
She took her kitten to the veterinarian for a checkup.

easy.def: Having to do with animal doctors.

more.def: Having to do with the care and medical treatment of animals.
examples: We took our cat to the veterinary clinic.
A veterinary nurse weighed the puppy.

easy.def: To say no to a plan or law.

more.def: To use your power to say no to a plan or law.
examples: Mom vetoed the idea of a puppy.
